withdrawnRecords.title: Environmental information: old wording kept after an EU correction
withdrawnRecords.statusDetail: Official guidance applies the EU definition
withdrawnRecords.summary: In 2022 the EU corrected the Danish text of its definition of environmental information. Denmark’s statute still uses the earlier words, but official guidance tells authorities to apply the EU definition.
withdrawnRecords.euChange: Article 2(1)(b) and (c) changed from factors or measures that affect or can affect the environment to those that affect or are likely to affect it.
withdrawnRecords.consequence: Yes, on paper. The Danish statute still defines environmental information with “can affect” where the corrected EU text says “are likely to affect”. This does not show that anyone’s access to information was reduced: official guidance applies the EU definition, and EU law permits wider national access.
withdrawnRecords.nationalGap: Consolidation Act 980 of 16 August 2017, § 3 nos 2–3, still uses the former Danish words. Denmark’s 2025 Aarhus implementation report explicitly acknowledges the divergence.
withdrawnRecords.nationalLaw: Miljøoplysningsloven, Consolidation Act 980 of 16 August 2017, § 3 nos 2–3; current official consolidation marked applicable.
withdrawnRecords.provisions: Directive 2003/4/EC Article 2(1)(b), (c); corrigendum OJ L 266, 13 October 2022, p. 22; national § 3 nos 2–3.
withdrawnRecords.resolution: A 2025 ministry report says the EU definition must govern despite the difference in words. The Ombudsman’s guide also points out the correction.
withdrawnRecords.caveat: A documented textual divergence, not an established breach or finding that access rights were reduced. Recital 24 permits wider national access. Conforming interpretation and the actual breadth of access require separate analysis. The corrigendum sets no fresh transposition deadline.
